speaker: Doctor
text: I'm Dr. Agent. To begin our assessment of your weakness and fatigue, have you been experiencing any fever, night sweats, or unintentional weight loss recently? Also, how would you describe the nature of your fatigue—is it constant or does it come and go?

speaker: Patient
text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. She mentions experiencing these symptoms currently. The patient has been traveling, hiking, and camping recently and notes having had multiple illnesses in the recent past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your recent hiking, camping, and multiple illnesses, have you noticed any specific insect bites, rash, or changes in your urine color? Also, has anyone around you been diagnosed with a similar illness recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of weakness, fatigue that worsens as the day progresses, and new-onset mild diplopia (double vision) is highly characteristic of this neuromuscular junction disorder. I recommend proceeding with acetylcholine receptor antibody testing and a repeatable clinical exam to confirm.
